specification.objective: Validate the #122 integration commit that combines the authenticated audit CSV hard limit from #113 with the already integrated accessible workspace skeleton behavior from #121, using main as the pre-integration baseline.

requirements.statement: The backend enforces an effective maximum CSV byte size no greater than 1 MiB before returning any CSV bytes and reports the exact matching row count and effective limit when over the ceiling; lower positive configuration values are supported.
An export exactly at the effective byte ceiling succeeds; an export one byte above it is rejected without a CSV body. Configured values above 1 MiB never raise the effective ceiling.
Over-limit feedback tells the user how many rows matched and the maximum file size, and asks them to narrow filters.
Authorization, company scope, applied filters, order, CSV columns and encoding remain identical.
One shared configurable skeleton primitive supports composable shapes, one animation controller per loading region, system reduced motion, theme colors, text scaling and responsive widths.
Route-session and Kanban skeletons reuse the shared primitive without changing their layout, keys or board rendering foundation.
Every ordinary content-loading spinner in Audit, Employees, Kanban, Projects/Tasks, time tracking and work-log task lists is replaced by a content-shaped skeleton.
Action submissions use disabled controls with accessible pending text/status and never use a content skeleton or spinner.
Workspace shell/navigation remains mounted; existing success, empty, error, retry, pagination, auth/revocation behavior and API contracts are preserved.
Skeleton regions expose one live announcement; decorative blocks are hidden from assistive technology; reduced motion stops animation and leaves no running ticker.
No dependency is added; only startup splash retains the CircularProgressIndicator, with the #113 audit export LinearProgressIndicator as its narrowly documented action-progress exception.
The #113 v1/v2 and #121 v2 locked contract files remain byte-for-byte identical to their source commits; this integration contract is additive and does not replace historical locks or proofs.

acceptance_criteria.statement: At the configured maximum size the authenticated export returns the complete CSV; one byte above returns a bounded error with exact count and limit, no CSV bytes.
A user holding audit.read sees a localized over-limit message with count and limit; the same endpoint continues to reject unauthorized users and exclude other tenants.
A shared primitive and region are reused by all migrated surfaces and route-session/Kanban skeletons.
Loading to success/empty/error remains usable and preserves scoped retry/pagination and workspace shell.
Reduced motion renders a static skeleton without a running ticker; animated regions use one controller; decorative blocks are excluded and the region label appears once.

Representative production ProjectTasksPage loading state is visually inspected at desktop and mobile browser viewports using a reproducible harness; responsive layout has no observed horizontal overflow.
Only the startup splash CircularProgressIndicator and narrowly contextualized audit-export LinearProgressIndicator remain; no added dependency or altered API contract.
Flutter analysis, focused and full test suites, build/smoke where available, git diff check, and complete diff review pass.
A repeatable browser harness renders the production ProjectTasksPage with a pending API response and retains the desktop/mobile visual inspection evidence.
The original #113 v1/v2 locked contracts match their source commit bytes, the #121 v2 locked contract matches main, and this new integration contract is a separate file.

invariants.statement: No company selector or permission bypass is introduced; request filters and authenticated company scope are unchanged.
The effective export ceiling is always at most 1 MiB, regardless of environment configuration.
Circular progress remains exclusively for cold-start server waiting; action pending states use disabled controls and accessible status.
API contracts, auth/revocation, existing loading/error/empty/retry/pagination semantics, and Kanban board rendering behavior do not change.
No external dependency is introduced; current workspace visual language and responsive behavior are preserved.
Do not modify or replace any existing #113/#121 contract lock or historical proof; the integration contract has its own baseline and identity.
The 1 MiB CSV ceiling and CSV authorization/company-scope invariants coexist with #121 skeleton behavior; export action progress remains the narrowly documented LinearProgressIndicator exception.

forbidden_states.statement: The server silently truncates an export or returns a partial CSV as if complete.
Ordinary in-app content loading uses a circular/refresh/Cupertino spinner.
Submission is represented by a misleading skeleton or inaccessible pending state.
Reduced motion leaves an active animation ticker or decorative blocks exposed to assistive technology.
No historical contract or proof is rewritten, removed, or re-baselined to make the integration validate.

inputs.statement: Existing authenticated audit export filters and server-configured byte ceiling.
Current content loading regions, their surrounding workspace shell, and accessible labels.

outputs.statement: Complete CSV within the byte ceiling, or a bounded over-limit error including exact matching row count and limit.
Reusable skeleton regions and page-specific skeleton compositions with preserved loading transitions.
An integrated source tree satisfying the #113 CSV size/security contract and the #121 skeleton/loading contract with original evidence preserved.

failure_semantics.statement: Oversize exports fail with HTTP 413 before CSV delivery; no partial file is downloaded.

If any ordinary content loading indicator remains outside the startup splash and the narrowly scoped audit export progress action, the source inventory regression exits nonzero and identifies the offending path/token.
Any failed configured gate, CSV security/limit regression, skeleton acceptance failure, or historical-lock byte mismatch blocks acceptance of this integration.
